title: Film Thickness Measurement - Overlay Shift Detection on Zeta-20
subtitle: Post-CMP Quality Validation for 10nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Yuki Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-20 system to detect and classify Overlay Shift defects during post-cmp inspection at the 10nm technology node. The test is conducted at Dresden Fab 3 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Overlay Shift defects that are critical to yield at the 10nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-20 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-20
- Inspection Type: Film Thickness Measurement
- Target Defect: Overlay Shift
- Process Step: Post-CMP
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 10nm
- Fab Location: Dresden Fab 3

This test case applies to all Zeta-20 systems deployed at Dresden Fab 3 for post-cmp monitoring in the 10nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-20
Software Version: v13.1.354
Recipe: FILM_THICKNESS_MEASUREMENT_10nm_POST_CMP
Illumination Mode: Brightfield
Scan Speed: Low (156 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.25μm
Edge Exclusion: 5mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-20 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Film Thickness Measurement' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Overlay Shift defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 10nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 107 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 95% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.6% for Film Thickness Measurement
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-08-05
Wafers Tested: 9
Total Defects Found: 4925
Defect Density: 1567.68 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 0.7%
Capture Rate: 86.2%
Test Duration: 97 minutes
System Uptime: 97.7%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-20 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Overlay Shift at the 10nm node.

b) The capture rate requires optimization of the detection algorithm.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) Recipe portability between systems at this fab was confirmed.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
